sources.publisher: Maine Emergency Services Communication Bureau / Maine GeoLibrary
Town of North Berwick / CAI Technologies

sources.usage: openly licensed photographs cropped and color-normalized into facades-atlas.webp; exact authors/licenses/source pages retained per atlas entry

transformations: All geographic vector geometry converted to a local meter coordinate system centered on North Berwick.
Residential address/location attributes are not copied from the Maine building-footprint layer.
Building heights are heuristic; named landmark styles supply minimum-height overrides only.
Named-road labels and street-sign intersection candidates are derived from Maine E911 road names.
Trees and utility poles are deterministic procedural scenery; they are not survey-grade asset locations.
Remote GIS/open-data services are build-time inputs only; generated game assets require no map/API calls at runtime.
Building footprints are reduced to oriented local frames so rooflines and facades follow the source footprint instead of axis-aligned blocks.
Road-facing sides are estimated from the nearest named Maine E911 road and used to place doors, windows, porches, parking, and landmark frontage.
Selected North Berwick facade photographs are cropped, color-normalized, packed into a 4 by 2 WebP atlas, and mapped only to corresponding authored/reference structures.
The combined facade atlas is distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0 with per-image attribution preserved in facades-atlas.json.

limitations: non-hero private residences are procedural approximations
modern commercial landmark dimensions and parking layouts are approximate unless directly supported by open source geometry/reference material
